messages:
alex_support: Heads up — ACME (private VPC) opened a ticket: tenant metrics stopped reporting to Console after an OIDC provider key rotation yesterday. console shows 0 events for tenant 'acme-prod' since 2024-01-12T14:00Z. correlation_id=cor-84a2

john_sre: Thanks. Any quick repro or logs? Did they change the auth proxy or sidecar config during the rotation?

alex_support: They said only rotation of the IdP keys (jwks) and we updated our OIDC client config. No other infra changes from customer side. I asked for sample request/response — they sent this: 

maya_customer: "curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://private.acme.example/v1/invoke"
# Response: 200 OK
# Body: { "result": "ok" }
# Console: no metrics ingested for tenant acme-prod since 14:00
# Response headers we can see: content-type, x-request-id. No x-tenant-id header forwarded.

devon_infra: Can you paste a decoded JWT (redact values) so we can confirm tenant claim is present?

maya_customer: sure — decoded payload shows: 
{
  "iss": "https://idp.acme.example/",
  "sub": "user:123",
  "tenant": "acme-prod",
  "iat": 1705040000,
  "exp": 1705043600
}

john_sre: Ok that suggests the tenant claim is in the token, but our sidecar/proxy is not mapping that claim into the X-Tenant-Id header that the ingestion path relies on. Two possibilities: 1) header-mapping rule was accidentally removed during the OIDC client update; 2) envoy filter that extracts claims from JWT is failing because jwks key id changed shape.

alex_support: They ran a quick test where they manually added the header and metrics started appearing: 

maya_customer: "curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Tenant-Id: acme-prod\" https://private.acme.example/v1/invoke"
# Console shows recent events for acme-prod right away.

devon_infra: Good repro. Can you share the sidecar logs for the JWT extraction flow? look for lines like "jwt->header map: tenant -> x-tenant-id" or errors about JWKS fetch.

maya_customer: Paste from sidecar logs (sanitized): 

[2024-01-12T14:01:02Z] INFO jwks: fetched keys from https://idp.acme.example/.well-known/jwks.json
[2024-01-12T14:01:03Z] WARN jwt-extract: claim mapping not configured, skipping claim->header injection
[2024-01-12T14:01:03Z] INFO request: id=req-9f1a route=/v1/invoke status=200

john_sre: That WARN is telling — the sidecar didn't have the mapping. Looks like during the client config update we missed applying the mapping block in the envoy config. I want to confirm what config they currently have. Ask them to cat the envoy filter config (or sidecar config map).

alex_support: They returned this snippet from their sidecar config map: 

```
jwt_claim_mappings: []
# previously: [{ claim: tenant, header: X-Tenant-Id }]
```

john_sre: There we go. Mapping is empty. Two action paths: (A) apply the mapping back and roll the sidecar (fast, immediate fix) or (B) issue a temporary rule on the ingress to set X-Tenant-Id from JWT claim using our ingress filter (works without sidecar change). Which do they prefer?

maya_customer: Fastest is A — they want minimal blast radius. Can you provide the exact patch we want them to apply?

devon_infra: Patch they need: 

```
jwt_claim_mappings:
  - claim: tenant
    header: X-Tenant-Id
```

Then restart sidecar pods or trigger a rolling restart of the service. That should restore header injection.

john_sre: Also advise them to validate JWKS caching TTL — if key rotation happens frequently, the fetch timing could make the extractor log transient errors. Add a health probe that checks claim->header mapping on startup. We'll add a guard in our next release to fail fast if mappings are empty for private installs.

alex_support: Shared patch with customer. They applied and rolled the sidecar; infra-bot shows a small deployment: 

infra-bot: deploy acme-sidecar v2.6.3 -> success (rolling): started 3 pods, ready=3

maya_customer: Confirming — metrics for acme-prod are back in Console as of 2024-01-12T14:07Z. Thanks! :tada:

john_sre: Great. Follow-ups: 1) we'll add a short KB article for customers who rotate IdP keys to remember the claim->header mapping; 2) SRE will add an automated check in our private installer that ensures jwt_claim_mappings is not empty when using tenant-based routing.

alex_support: I'll update the ticket with steps and close after we publish the KB. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
